real_conflicts: The 'Visual System Craft' proposal to remove the background box and shadow from the 'Recommended Actions' list is rejected. Removing the container would cause the white text to disappear against the dark background and the blue chart bars, destroying legibility. The text requires a high-contrast container to be readable, so it must remain a distinct visual object.

The 'Expressiveness' proposal to add a 'wave motif' or 'topographic map' background is rejected. The current layout is already struggling with density; adding complex background textures will reduce the contrast of the data lines and text, making the chart harder to read. Clarity must take precedence over decorative storytelling.
accepted: The 'Brief Intent' proposal to move the 'Recommended Actions' panel to the bottom right corner is accepted. This clears the occlusion of the 'Precipitation Intensity' chart, allowing the data bars to be fully visible and legible.

The 'Brief Intent' proposal to ensure the 'High-Risk Districts' list does not overlap the X-axis labels is accepted. The timeline labels (J, F, M...) are critical for reading the temperature trend and must remain unobstructed.
concession: I concede that the current 'floating modal' aesthetic is visually noisy and contributes to the clutter. While I insist the text needs a background for contrast, I agree that the heavy drop shadow and rounded corners are unnecessary and can be simplified to a flatter, sharper style to better fit the editorial grid.
compromise: Relocate the 'Recommended Actions' panel to the bottom right corner (below the Sea Level Rise card) and the 'High-Risk Districts' list to the bottom center. Retain the dark background box for the 'Recommended Actions' to ensure text legibility, but remove the heavy drop shadow and rounded corners to integrate it more cleanly into the grid.
nonnegotiable: No text element may overlap or obscure data visualization elements (bars, lines, or axis labels). The reader must be able to see the full extent of the precipitation bars and the temperature timeline without visual interference.
